title: Self-direction 1: observe

D0.outcome: Explains that observing means noting what happened before judging it.

D1.outcome: After the first game, marks one moment he was unsure and states what he expected the opponent to do.

D2.outcome: After three consecutive games, marks an unsure moment and his expectation of the opponent unprompted, each specific to that game.

D3.outcome: After a game, compares his expectation with what the opponent actually did and says so in one sentence.

misconceptions: Reflection means saying whether I played well.
sources: docs/first-hours.md session 3 (reflection before engine commentary), 'What would show this does or doesn't work'
conditions: The reflection comes before any engine commentary.
contrasts: An empty or generic answer ('it was fine'): the prompt is too abstract and needs a concrete question.
Reflecting after engine output, which anchors the answer.
A game of three moves ending in a disconnect.
contrast_sources: FH, what would show this does not work
note: A played game is a session milestone, not a node; D1 depends on FND.CAPTURE.D1 as the weakest rules prerequisite.
